Per the party tables released with the UMich survey, independents’ expectations jumped 10.7 points to 52.8, the highest since December 2025, and Democrats’ rose 7.1 to 42.4, the highest since January 2025. Meanwhile Republicans’ fell 11.6 points to 76.6, the lowest since October 2024, before the last presidential election.

That cut the gap between Republican and Democratic expectations to 34.2 points from 52.9, the narrowest since November 2024. 

Independents’ overall sentiment rose to 51.4 from 42.4, the highest since September 2025. The national numbers have tracked independents closely according to a May special report.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
#UMich University of Michigan consumer sentiment moves to 51.5 in the final November read (preliminary 51.0; October 48.0), the highest since August, as the midterms lifted expectations and inflation expectations plunged.

▪️ Expectations were revised up to 52.9, the highest since July, but current conditions were revised down to 49.4.
▪️ Per survey director Joanne Hsu, expectations “surged for independents” (up 10.7 points) and rose for Democrats (up 7.1), but fell 11.6 points for Republicans to the lowest since October 2024, the biggest election-month swing in party data covering midterms back to 2006.
▪️ Year-ahead inflation expectations “plunged” to 3.7% from 4.7%, the lowest since February and the biggest one-month drop since June 2025, as gas prices fell.
▪️ Long-run expectations fell to 3.3%, tying June through August for the lowest since March.
▪️ Sentiment still “remains subdued at 9% below February,” before the Iran conflict, and is below every reading before 2022.

Copper just had its worst week since July 2025. Front-month /HG futures fell 9.9% to close Friday at $5.49/lb. That leaves copper about 21% below September’s record intraday high, which puts it in a bear market by the usual definition.

The chart damage is significant:

▪️ Earlier this month copper closed below the uptrend from the August 2025 low, which had held through the spring 2026 lows. This week’s drop leaves it about 11% below that line.
▪️ On a chart going back to late 2022, only two weeks were worse: April 2025 (about −14%) and July 2025 (about −23%, when refined copper was exempted from the 50% tariff).
▪️ The next major support is $4.90 to $5.00. That’s where the long-term uptrend from the October 2023 low sits, and it has held at every test since (February and November 2024, January and August 2025).

Evercore ISI says copper, as a proxy for the AI buildout, has been falling alongside the Nasdaq 100 since the October peak. They note that past bubble bursts (2000, and Japan in 1989) saw stocks, bond yields, oil and copper all fall together. Their key level: a copper “Soft Landing” above “AI Revolution” bull market support at that $5/lb level noted earlier.

$5 then appears to be the level to watch. That's another 9% lower.  A weekly close below it would break a trend that has held since late 2023.

The VIX closed at 35.9 on Friday’s monthly options expiration, its highest on an expiration day since April 2020.

Since 1990, there have been 30 expirations with the VIX at 30 or higher. What the S&P 500 did next (vs. all days):

▪ First week: a coin flip, higher about half the time.
▪ One month: median +4.4%, higher 77% of the time (all days +1.2%, 64%).
▪ Six months: median +17.4%, higher in 28 of 30 (all days +5.7%, 75%).
▪ The catch: the median worst close within three months was −4.9%, and in September 2008 the index fell 21.5% in a month.

Counting only the first expiration in each run (12 cases), the S&P 500 was higher six months later 11 of 12 times.
